increments.title: The context panel gets a working block filter
increments.goal: Give the context panel head a dropdown that lists the block kinds and top-level fields the shown request actually contains, and let the reader hide and show them, against the record the panel already holds.
criteria: The context panel head carries a dropdown built as a `<details>` popover, with no framework and no new dependency, listing every block kind and every top-level field the currently shown request actually contains, one checkbox each, with the number of blocks behind that entry (e.g. `tool_result 12`).

The list is in two labelled groups: **Blocks** first, holding the block kinds present (`assistant`, `other`, `raw`, `system`, `thinking`, `tool_result`, `tool_use`, `user`) sorted alphabetically; then **Fields**, holding the body's remaining top-level keys (`max_tokens`, `metadata`, `model`, `tools`, …) sorted alphabetically. Entries are labelled by the kind name and the field key verbatim, so `system` and `tools` read as one list.
The dropdown holds two buttons, **all on** and **all off**. *All on* makes every entry visible. *All off* hides every entry the currently shown request contains.

Unchecking an entry removes its blocks from the list below; checking it puts them back. Neither triggers a fetch: the filter is applied to the record the panel already holds, and `/api/content/at` is not called again.

The selection is one page-wide state, held as the set of *hidden* entries. It survives a lane change, a scrub, a live refresh and a session change; it is not persisted and a page reload starts with everything visible. An entry never hidden is visible, which is what makes an entry that appears for the first time — a `thinking` block in a later request, a field an earlier body did not carry — arrive visible, including after *all off* was pressed on a request that did not contain it.
An entry the current request does not contain is not listed, and its hidden state is remembered: scrubbing to a request that carries it again shows it still unchecked and its blocks still hidden.

The derivation and the markup are pure functions in `public/context.js` — no `document`, no `fetch`, no `location`, the contract `test/independence.test.mjs` guards — and only the click wiring lives in `app.js`.
The filter's markup carries no `data-lane` attribute and its `<summary>` carries no `data-block`, so opening the dropdown neither toggles the lane selection nor a block's expansion.
An open dropdown survives a repaint: a live refresh that re-renders `#lane-panel` does not snap it shut, the same way `state.expanded` keeps expanded blocks open today.
`npm --prefix tools/argus-ui test` passes after this increment, and each criterion above has at least one test that goes red when its behaviour is broken or removed.
increments.note: Accepted in review round 1: the context panel's filter is built as pure functions in public/context.js with only the click and change wiring in app.js, and the whole suite runs 230 cases at exit 0.

increments.title: The panel head names visible and total, and the empty case says so
increments.goal: Make the filtered panel tell the truth about how much it is hiding: the head names visible-of-total blocks and characters, and a panel with everything hidden shows a placeholder instead of an empty list.
criteria: With nothing hidden, the head line reads as it does today (`210.114 chars · 34 blocks`). With something hidden it names both numbers — visible of total — for blocks and for characters, so the filter can never make a context look smaller than it is. The totals stay readable off `data-chars` and `data-blocks`; the visible counts arrive in data attributes of their own.
With every entry hidden the panel keeps its `data-state="ready"` and shows a placeholder in place of the rows, saying every kind is hidden and where to turn them back on.

The head's new numbers and the placeholder are derived and rendered by pure functions in `public/context.js`, under the contract `test/independence.test.mjs` guards; no new wiring is needed in `app.js` for either.

The cases the previous increment wrote to pin today's behaviour — that a partly filtered panel leaves the head's totals untouched, and that an all-hidden panel renders an empty block list with no placeholder — are updated to the new behaviour in the same change, so no case is left red, skipped or asserting the superseded shape.
`npm --prefix tools/argus-ui test` passes over the whole suite after this increment, and each criterion above has at least one test that goes red when its behaviour is broken or removed.
increments.note: Criteria sharpened after filter-core: two of its cases deliberately pin the head's totals and the placeholder-less all-hidden panel, so updating them is part of this increment rather than a surprise red suite. Added that this increment needs no new app.js wiring, which filter-core's delivery showed.

return.summary: Add a pure contextCounts() to public/context.js and use it in renderContextPanel so a filtered head names visible-of-total blocks and characters in its line and in two data attributes of its own, and an all-hidden request renders one placeholder in place of the block list while the panel stays data-state="ready".
return.plan:
Make the filtered context panel tell the truth about what it hides. One production file changes: tools/argus-ui/public/context.js. Do not touch public/app.js, public/styles.css or public/index.html — the wiring and the CSS this increment needs already exist (app.js already passes `hidden` and `filterOpen` into `lanePanelInput`, and `.placeholder` is already styled). WHAT GETS BUILT 1. A new exported pure function in public/context.js, placed in the "the filter" section directly after `visibleBlocks` and before `contextEntryIds`: export function contextCounts({ blocks = [], chars = 0, hidden = [] } = {}) It returns { chars, blocks, visibleChars, visibleBlocks, filtered } where - `chars` is the `chars` argument verbatim (the whole body's length, what `contextBlocks` returns and what `data-chars` already carries), - `blocks` is `blocks.length`, the total block count, - `visibleBlocks` is `visibleBlocks(blocks, hidden).length`, - `visibleChars` is the sum of the `chars` field of exactly those visible blocks, - `filtered` is `visibleBlocks !== blocks` — true only when this record actually lost a block. It mutates neither argument, accepts `hidden` as an array or a Set (reuse the existing `visibleBlocks` helper, which already normalises it), and returns all zeroes for no arguments at all. The object-argument form matches `renderContextFilter` and `lanePanelInput`; the return keys map one-to-one onto the data attributes below, which is why the count field is named `blocks` even though the input `blocks` is an array — name the local array something else inside the body. 2. `renderContextPanel` uses it for the head. Today the head line is [fmtClock(item.timeMs), item.model, `${fmtNum(chars)} chars`, `${blocks.length} blocks`] joined by ' · ' after esc. Keep that shape and swap the last two parts when, and only when, `counts.filtered` is true: - chars part: `${fmtNum(counts.visibleChars)} of ${fmtNum(counts.chars)} chars` - blocks part: `${counts.visibleBlocks} of ${counts.blocks} blocks` Both parts keep going through the same `.map(esc).join(' · ')` as today. The word between the two numbers is `of`, lower case, with single spaces. 3. The two new data attributes ride on the same `` as `data-chars` and `data-blocks`, are named `data-visible-chars` and `data-visible-blocks`, carry the raw integers through `esc`, and are rendered only when `counts.filtered` is true. `data-chars` and `data-blocks` keep the record's own totals in every case — the filter never rewrites them. 4. The all-hidden placeholder. When `blocks.length > 0` and the visible list is empty, `renderContextPanel` renders, in place of the whole `
…
` container, exactly:
Every kind in this request is hidden. Turn them back on in the filter above.
The head, its totals and the filter dropdown are unchanged and still rendered, and the shell stays `shell('ready', …)` so `data-state="ready"` holds. The text carries no apostrophe and no angle bracket, so it survives `esc` unchanged; put it through `esc` anyway, the way the other two placeholders are. Reuse the bare `class="placeholder"` — no new class and no new CSS rule. DECISIONS AND WHAT THEY WERE CHOSEN OVER - `visibleChars` is the sum of the visible blocks' own `chars`, not `chars` minus the hidden blocks' chars. Rejected because the block texts do not add up to the body: for the suite's own fixture the twelve blocks carry 396 characters against a 770-character body, the rest being JSON scaffolding that belongs to no block. Subtracting would make an all-hidden panel claim 374 visible characters with zero rows on screen, which is the exact lie this increment exists to prevent. The chosen definition gives 0 there, and it is the number a reader can add up from the `data-chars` on the rows. The consequence to accept: with nothing hidden the visible sum (396) is still below the total (770), which is why the visible numbers are rendered only when something is actually hidden — with nothing hidden the head is byte-for-byte today's. - `filtered` keys on a block actually removed, never on `hidden` being non-empty. A hidden id the current request does not carry must leave the markup byte-identical to the unfiltered render — an existing case ('an entry hidden but absent from this request changes nothing…') asserts that equality and must keep passing. - The placeholder is rendered inline by `renderContextPanel` rather than by a new exported render function: `renderContextPanel` is already the pure renderer the criterion asks for, and a second export would widen the surface for one string. - The placeholder is gated on `blocks.length > 0`. A request that simply has no blocks (`{"messages":[]}`) keeps rendering today's empty `
` — nothing is hidden there, so nothing may claim it is. - `data-chars` stays the body length, so the head's two chars numbers are measured differently (visible = sum of block texts, total = body length). Say so in the JSDoc of `contextCounts`: the visible count never adds up to the total because the body's JSON scaffolding belongs to no block, which is precisely why the total is printed beside it and never replaced. STYLE THE FILE KEEPS Every exported function in public/context.js carries a JSDoc block with `@param`/`@returns` and a sentence on why it is shaped the way it is; inline comments explain the decision, not the mechanics. Follow it for `contextCounts` and for the placeholder branch. No `document`, no `fetch(`, no `location.` may appear in this module — `test/independence.test.mjs` greps for them.

return.testPlan:
Tests are needed. Everything in this increment is a pure function's output, and all of it is checkable in one file.

WHERE, WITH WHAT, AND IN WHOSE STYLE

Every case below goes in /home/user/uroboros/tools/argus-ui/test/context.test.mjs. Framework: `node:test` with `node:assert/strict`, ESM, no runner config. Run just this file from the repository root with:

  node --test tools/argus-ui/test/context.test.mjs

Conventions of that file, which the new cases follow:
- Imports at the top: `import test from 'node:test'; import assert from 'node:assert/strict';` then a single named import block from `'../public/context.js'` (lines 4-15) and one from `'../public/format.js'`. Add `contextCounts` to the first block; `visibleBlocks`, `contextEntryIds` and `contextBlocks` are already imported, and `fmtNum` and `esc` come from the second.
- All input comes from the four factories at lines 21-64 — `requestBody(over)`, `item(over)`, `lane(over)`, `view(over)` — each taking an override object spread last. Never build a body inline; call `requestBody({ messages: […] })`.
- `blockChunks(html)` (line 79) returns the rendered `<details class="ctx-block">…</details>` chunks in order; use it for anything about the row list.
- Test names are lower-case sentences describing the behaviour ('unchecking an entry removes its blocks below and only unchecks that box'), never 'should …'. Every assertion carries a message saying what a failure means, in the same voice.
- Numbers are derived in the test where they can be — the file writes `requestBody().length` and `contextBlocks(requestBody()).blocks` rather than literals, while hard-coding the block count 12. Do the same: derive character sums from `contextBlocks(requestBody()).blocks`, and keep 12 as the literal total block count.
- Nothing is faked or stubbed: these are pure functions called directly. The only fake in the file is the `recorder()` api function, which none of these cases needs.
- Put the new cases at the end of the file under one banner comment naming this increment, in the style of the existing `// Increment 5 — …` banners.

Fixture facts, for cross-checking (do not paste them as the expectations): `requestBody()` is 770 characters and yields 12 blocks whose own texts total 396 characters; the single `tool_result` block is 12 of those. So a panel with `kind:tool_result` hidden shows 11 of 12 blocks and 384 of 770 characters.

THE CASES

Criterion 1 — with nothing hidden the head reads as today; with something hidden it names visible of total for blocks and for characters; the totals stay on data-chars and data-blocks; the visible counts arrive in data attributes of their own.

1. 'the counts of an unfiltered record are its own totals' — unit, `contextCounts`. Input: `contextBlocks(requestBody())`'s `blocks` and `chars`, `hidden: []`. Expect `{ chars: requestBody().length, blocks: 12, visibleBlocks: 12, visibleChars: <sum of every block's chars, reduced in the test>, filtered: false }` by `assert.deepEqual`. Assert in the same case that that sum is strictly below `requestBody().length`, with a message saying the body's JSON scaffolding belongs to no block — without it the following cases cannot tell the two definitions of `visibleChars` apart and the suite goes vacuous.
2. 'hiding one entry takes its blocks and its characters out of the visible counts' — unit, `contextCounts` with `hidden: ['kind:tool_result']`. Expect `visibleBlocks` 11, `visibleChars` equal to the reduced sum minus the tool_result block's own `chars`, `filtered` true, and `chars`/`blocks` still the record's totals.
3. 'an id the record does not carry hides nothing and does not count as filtered' — unit, edge. `contextCounts` over the fixture with `hidden: ['kind:thinking', 'field:absent']` against a body built as `requestBody({ messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'hi' }] })` (no thinking block, no such field). Expect `filtered: false`, `visibleBlocks` equal to `blocks`, `visibleChars` equal to that record's own block sum.
4. 'every entry hidden leaves nothing visible at all' — unit, edge/limit. `hidden: contextEntryIds(item())` over the fixture's blocks. Expect `visibleBlocks: 0`, `visibleChars: 0`, `filtered: true`, and `chars`/`blocks` still the totals.
5. 'the counts hold with no arguments and with a Set' — unit, edge/empty and repeat. `assert.deepEqual(contextCounts(), { chars: 0, blocks: 0, visibleChars: 0, visibleBlocks: 0, filtered: false })`, and `contextCounts` given `hidden` as `new Set(['kind:user'])` must deep-equal the same call given `['kind:user']`.
6. 'with nothing hidden the head line and its attributes are exactly what they were' — integration over `renderContextPanel({ lane: lane(), item: item() })`. Assert the meta span still matches `data-chars="<requestBody().length>"` and `data-blocks="12"`, that the readable line still carries `` `${fmtNum(requestBody().length)} chars` `` and `12 blocks`, that the whole markup contains neither `data-visible-chars` nor `data-visible-blocks`, and that the meta span carries no ` of ` — the head of an unfiltered panel says nothing about a filter.
7. Rewrite the existing case at line 984, 'unchecking an entry removes its blocks below and only unchecks that box'. Its block-list and checkbox assertions stay as they are. Its two head assertions (lines 1005-1010) keep asserting `data-blocks="12"` and `data-chars="<requestBody().length>"` — those totals are still the required behaviour — but their messages must lose the superseded 'the filter does not own that number yet' and say instead that the totals are what stops the filter making the context look smaller than it is. Add to the same case, or to a new case named 'a filtered head names the visible numbers beside the totals' fed the same `hidden: ['kind:tool_result']` input: `data-visible-blocks="11"`, `data-visible-chars="<derived>"`, and the readable line containing `11 of 12 blocks` and `` `${fmtNum(visibleChars)} of ${fmtNum(requestBody().length)} chars` ``. Whichever shape you pick, no assertion carrying the superseded message may survive in the file.
8. Do not weaken the existing case at line 1051, 'an entry hidden but absent from this request changes nothing and is not listed, and its hidden state is remembered'. Its byte-for-byte equality is what pins criterion 1's other half — a request that lost no block renders exactly the unfiltered head. It must keep passing untouched. The same holds for the equality at lines 1012-1016 (`hidden: []` renders what no `hidden` renders) and for 'the head names the lane and the record the context came from' (line 309).

Criterion 2 — with every entry hidden the panel keeps data-state="ready" and shows a placeholder in place of the rows, saying every kind is hidden and where to turn them back on.

9. Extend the existing case at line 1038, 'everything hidden leaves an empty list but a reader can still turn entries back on'. Keep its four assertions (no block chunks, `data-state="ready"`, ten entries still listed, no checkbox checked) and add: exactly one `class="placeholder"` in the markup; no `<div class="ctx-blocks">` container at all; the placeholder's own text matching `/hidden/` and `/filter/` so a placeholder that names neither the state nor the way out fails; and `data-visible-blocks="0"` on the meta span. Rename the case to say a placeholder replaces the rows.
10. 'a request with no blocks at all shows no all-hidden placeholder' — integration, edge/empty. `renderContextPanel({ lane: lane(), item: item({ body: '{"messages":[]}' }) })`. Expect `data-state="ready"`, no `class="placeholder"` anywhere, and the empty `<div class="ctx-blocks">` container still present — nothing is hidden here, so nothing may say it is. Note the sibling case at line 1112 already uses this body for the filter's own absence; leave it alone.
11. 'a placeholder for no record is still the record placeholder' — integration, guard. The existing cases at lines 347 and 354 already pin `data-state="empty"` with exactly one placeholder and `data-state="pending"` with no blocks; add nothing, and do not touch them.

Criterion 3 — the new numbers and the placeholder are derived and rendered by pure functions in public/context.js, under the contract test/independence.test.mjs guards, with no new wiring in app.js.

12. No new case. `test/independence.test.mjs`'s third case already greps public/context.js for `document.`, `fetch(` and `location.` and goes red the moment the new code reaches for one, and every case above calls the new code as an import of that module, which is what makes 'pure function in context.js' the only way to pass them. The 'no new wiring' half is an absence in app.js: page.test.mjs already pins that `renderLanePanel` passes `hidden` and `filterOpen` through, and an assertion that app.js gained nothing else would pin the shape of a file this increment does not open.

DELIBERATELY UNTESTED

- The CSS. `.placeholder` is an existing rule and the markup adds no class; no case in this suite reads styles.css, and adding one for this would test the stylesheet's text rather than any behaviour.
- The exact wording of the placeholder sentence. The cases pin that it names the hidden state and the filter, not the copy, so rewording it stays a free edit.
- `fmtNum`'s own thresholds. They are covered where `fmtNum` is defined and tested; here the expectations call `fmtNum` rather than restating what it prints, so a change to the formatter cannot make these cases lie.
- The browser. There is no DOM test in this project; every rendering case asserts on the returned HTML string, as the whole file does.

WHAT IS ALREADY RED

Nothing is known red. I ran no test — not the suite and not one file — so the first run is the implementer's. The one command I did run was a `node -e` one-liner importing public/context.js to measure the fixture (770 body characters, 12 blocks, 396 characters of block text), which settled the definition of `visibleChars` recorded in the plan; it ran no test and exercised no changed code.

increments.title: The tools box under the timeline goes, its tick marks stay
increments.goal: Delete the redundant tool list panel and the per-call parameter ballast it forced into page state, while leaving every other tool signal on the timeline exactly as it is.
criteria: `public/tools.js` and `test/tools.test.mjs` are deleted, and `app.js` imports neither `laneToolInput` nor `renderToolPanel`.
`renderLanePanel()` paints only the context panel into `#lane-panel`.

Everything else about tools on the timeline is untouched: the `data-kind="tool"` tick marks on the lane track, the `data-tools` count in each lane's meta, the `tool call` legend entry, and the incremental `/api/events?event=claude_code.tool_result` poll with its `sinceSeq` watermark.

`toolCallOf()` keeps only what a mark needs — `seq`, `timeMs`, `spanId` — and no longer derives or holds `name`, `preview`, `text`, `chars` or `truncated`. `TOOL_PARAM_CHARS` and the `paramText()` helper go with it. `mergeToolMarks()` keeps its contract: duplicates dropped by `seq`, the watermark returned as the highest `seq` actually held, the input array untouched.
The context panel and its filter come through unchanged: the panel is still built from one input builder, and the filter still renders, hides and reopens exactly as the earlier increments left it.

Every case outside the deleted file that asserts the old tool-mark shape or the tool panel's presence — whole-object assertions on `toolCallOf()`'s return among them — is updated or removed in the same change, so no case is left red, skipped or asserting the superseded shape.
`npm --prefix tools/argus-ui test` passes over the whole suite after this increment, and each criterion above has at least one test that goes red when its behaviour is broken or removed.
increments.note: Added two criteria after filter-core: that increment's one rejected round was caused entirely by older whole-object assertions left pinning a superseded shape, and this increment narrows a whole-object shape too. Also pinned that the context panel and its filter survive the deletion, since both now share `renderLanePanel()`.

increments.title: The six technical tabs go out of the code
increments.goal: Remove the pre-timeline tab interface — its views, its state, its wiring and its per-refresh fetches — and land the whole issue with both suites green.
criteria: `DETAIL_VIEWS` and `renderDetailViews()` are gone from `public/timeline.js`, and no tab nav is rendered anywhere.

Gone from `public/app.js`: `renderTabBody()`, `renderOverviewTab()`, `renderTodosTab()`, `renderTracesTab()`, `renderWaterfall()`, `renderSpanInspector()`, `renderEventsTab()`, `renderMetricsTab()`, `renderRawTab()`, `loadTabData()`, the helpers only they used (`kpi`, `formatValue`, `spanKind`, `spanNote`, `todoStatusChip`, `SPAN_KINDS`), the `#tab-body` container, and the state fields `tab`, `trace`, `selectedTraceId`, `selectedSpanId`, `events`, `eventFilters`, `metrics`, `facets`.

Gone from the wiring in `wireEvents()`: the handlers for `[data-tab]`, `[data-trace]`, `[data-span]` and `[data-event-seq]`, the `change` handler for `event-filter` and `event-errors`, and the `event-search` branch of the `input` handler. The 15-second interval no longer repaints a tab body.
`renderDetail()` no longer builds the `counts` object, and no refresh requests `/api/traces`, `/api/facets` or `/api/metrics`. The `/api/events` request that feeds the tool marks stays.
No unused import or dead helper is left behind in `app.js` or `timeline.js`, and the tests that pinned the removed views are removed with them rather than left skipped.

The `change` and `input` listeners the context filter and the rest of the page still need survive the removal: the filter's checkboxes, the *all on* and *all off* buttons and the lane selection all still work.
`src/server.mjs` is unchanged: it proxies `/api/*` blindly and knows no route by name.
`npm --prefix tools/argus-ui test` is green over the whole suite, and each criterion above has at least one test that goes red when its behaviour is broken or removed.
`./test.sh` is green.
increments.note: Two changes: the suite criterion now asks for this increment's own criteria to be covered rather than the whole issue's, since every earlier increment already carries its own coverage criterion; and a criterion was added that the shared `change` and `input` listeners the filter depends on survive, because filter-core put the filter's wiring into exactly those handlers.

return.summary: Closed filter-core as done (accepted in review round 1, suite 230 cases exit 0) and re-cut the three open increments against what it showed. The cut and its order are unchanged — filter-honesty, then tools-box, then tabs-out — because the risky part, the filter itself, is already delivered and each remaining increment is one coherent deliverable that leaves the repository working. What changed is the criteria, and one lesson drove most of it: filter-core's only rejected round was caused entirely by older whole-object assertions still pinning a shape the increment superseded, which cost a full correction chain. So every remaining increment that narrows or changes a pinned shape now carries an explicit criterion that those cases are updated or removed in the same change rather than left red or skipped: filter-honesty for the two cases filter-core wrote to pin today's head totals and the placeholder-less all-hidden panel, tools-box for the whole-object assertions on toolCallOf's return and anything asserting the tool panel's presence. Two further additions come from where filter-core put its wiring: tools-box now pins that the context panel and its filter come through the deletion of the tool box unchanged, since both now share renderLanePanel(), and tabs-out now pins that the shared change and input listeners the filter's checkboxes and its all on/all off buttons live in survive the removal of the tab handlers. filter-honesty gained a criterion that its numbers and placeholder stay pure functions in context.js needing no new app.js wiring, which filter-core's delivery showed to be achievable. tabs-out's suite criterion was narrowed from 'every criterion of the issue' to its own criteria, because every increment now carries its own coverage criterion and asking the last one to re-verify the others gives one criterion two owners. Nothing was split, merged or dropped: filter-honesty is small but coherent and belongs to nothing else, and the two deletions are separate deliverables that each stand alone.
